description: Analog Horror (or Analogue Horror ) is a subgenre of Found Footage horror that emerged primarily on the internet in the mid-to-late 2010s. [ 1 ] It features horror elements within media designed to emulate outdated "analog" formats from the late 20th century, such as VHS tapes, television broadcasts, emergency alerts (EAS), and public access television. This aesthetic evokes feelings of dread, fear, and uncanniness by corrupting familiar or seemingly mundane media with unsettling content, often without visible protagonists. The genre builds suspense by starting videos normally before slowly introducing disturbing elements, frequently relying on ambiguous storytelling.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Unsettling the familiar, loss of control, fear of malfunctioning technology, questioning authority, cosmic horror
